items.headline: US convenience stores warn SNAP stocking rule could reduce food access
items.summary: Convenience-store groups warned USDA that a new SNAP stocking rule could strain compliance for 117,000 U.S. stores and reduce food access in rural and underserved areas, according to AgroLatam.
items.uncertainty_note: Item-level editorial approval only; wording must remain limited to retained evidence.
items.why_it_matters: U.S. SNAP stocking-rule story contains concrete rural/underserved food-access risk; wording restrained to a warning/proposal.

items.headline: San Antonio SNAP households can seek replacement benefits after storm food loss
items.summary: KSAT reported that SNAP recipients who lost food when a Friday storm knocked out power could seek replacement benefits through a San Antonio Food Bank-supported process.
items.uncertainty_note: Item-level editorial approval only; wording must remain limited to retained evidence.
items.why_it_matters: San Antonio SNAP replacement-benefit story documents storm-related food loss and a bounded relief path.

items.headline: Gary families report denied SNAP replacement claims after power-outage food loss
items.summary: The 19th reported that Gary families lost weeks of food during a power outage and had SNAP replacement claims denied, leaving households unable to replace spoiled food.
items.uncertainty_note: Item-level editorial approval only; wording must remain limited to retained evidence.
items.why_it_matters: Gary power-outage story documents families losing food they could not afford to replace and denied SNAP replacement claims.

items.headline: SNAP cuts could threaten free school meals for millions of children

items.headline: Palm Springs food bank displacement halts weekly aid for 250 families
items.summary: Hoodline reported that a Palm Springs fire-station project displaced Well in the Desert from its longtime site, halting weekly food-bank help to 250 families.
